sentences.text: Tianyuraptor is a short-armed dromaeosaurid dinosaur closely related to birds.
The holotype specimen, STM1–3, is a nearly complete skeleton missing only the very tip of the tail.
The fossil preserves 25 fully articulated tail vertebrae, with at most three more estimated to be missing from the end.
Unlike many other theropods from the Jehol Group, the Tianyuraptor holotype preserves no soft tissues.
The forelimbs are unusually short, measuring only 53% of the length of its hindlimbs.
The tail is relatively long, measuring 960 mm and nearly 4.8 times the length of the femur.
Fossils of Tianyuraptor were discovered in western Liaoning, China.
The specific name ostromi honors John Ostrom, a significant contributor to the study of dromaeosaurid fossils.
In 2013, Agnolín and Novas interpreted Tianyuraptor as an averaptoran of uncertain position.
Tianyuraptor lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 122 million years ago.

The specific rock layer where Tianyuraptor fossils were found, the Dawangzhangzi Bed, is dated to about 122 million years ago, which falls within the broader age range of the Yixian Formation (approximately 129.7 to 122.1 million years ago) and corresponds to the Barremian to Aptian stages (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago).
It is debated whether Tianyuraptor is a basal microraptorine or a basal member of the clade containing other Laurasian dromaeosaurids.
